messages:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT ALERT: high tail latency detected for /v1/generate on shared-gpu-pool-2 - p95=4200ms p99=9800ms. Paging @oncall
Sam T: seeing it on the dashboard. streaming stalls flagged on a subset of requests. rolling p95 spike started ~1739123400
Priya R: I’m on it, grabbing flamegraphs and pod metrics. any obvious deploys? deploy-bot: auto-deploy check: no deploys in last 30m
Alex M: checking node IO and GPU utilization. Iops for pool-2 are high (~95th percentile). cgroup memory pressure? not yet
Jordan L: can you paste top processes on the host? suspect noisy-tenant
Maya S: adding tail logs for streaming worker 7
Sam T: stack traces show long waits in nv_peer_mem and occasional NVML timeouts
Priya R: capturing `nvidia-smi pmon -c 1` and `iostat -x 1 5` now
Alex M: quick glance — one pod (tenant-453) is showing sustained 100% GPU SM utilization + huge pinned memory growth
Sam T: tenant-453 is on burst tier (multi-tenant shared pool). Could be a runaway job
Leah C (CS): any customer impact? we have a support ticket for slow responses from acme-inc
Sam T: confirmed increased 5xx retries from acme-inc and long streaming stalls. CS ticket updated
Priya R: mitigation options: 1) cgroup cpu/gpu throttle for tenant-453 2) evict that pod to another node 3) apply per-tenant token-bucket rate limit
Alex M: we can test a soft throttle first to avoid immediate evict; patch cgroup gpu quota via runtime shim
Jordan L: how quickly can we apply throttle and measure? need to keep within SLA if possible
Maya S: I can run the throttle command. sample command for the runtime shim:
```
# throttle tenant container to 40% GPU time
runtime-shimctl set-quota --tenant tenant-453 --gpu-quota 40
```
Maya S: applying now (testing on one replica)
ops-bot: action logged: Maya S ran runtime-shimctl at 1739123512
Sam T: metrics: within 30s we see tenant-453 GPU utilization drop from 98% -> 42%
Priya R: p95 for /v1/generate on pool-2 dropping from 4200ms -> 850ms after throttle
Alex M: p99 still elevated ~1500ms but trending down. still seeing a handful of streaming stalls (maybe connection backlog)
Jordan L: can we bump kernel io scheduler on the affected node? or move tenant to dedicated gpu pool?
Maya S: evicting one replica of tenant-453 to dedicated-gpu-1 to see if it heals. `kubectl drain --pod-selector=tenant=tenant-453 --to-node=dedicated-gpu-1` (dry-run -> no disruption)
Sam T: traffic shaping + eviction successful for 1 replica. overall tail latency now p95=720ms p99=1200ms
Leah C (CS): updated acme-inc: we detected elevated latency affecting some requests; mitigation in progress, will follow up in 30m
Priya R: adding temporary autoscaling policy: limit tenant-453 concurrent streams to 6 via rate-limit config
Alex M: also increased KV cache TTL for common prefixes to reduce conditioning work
ops-bot: incident severity escalated to Sev2 at 1739123540 due to customer impact
Sam T: timeline so far: start 1739123400 alert -> throttle 1739123512 -> eviction 1739123560 -> steadying 1739123620
Jordan L: root cause hypothesis: noisy neighbor causing GPU SM saturation + IO pressure (large batch/reductions causing PCIe stalls). We'll need postmortem with kernel traces and cgroup metrics
Maya S: collecting `perf` and `nvidia-smi --query` dumps, saving to /var/ops/incidents/1739123456
Priya R: recommended follow-ups: 1) enforce per-tenant GPU quotas at admission 2) implement eviction thresholds on IO contention 3) add automatic fallback to lower-capacity model variant when p99 > 1.5s
Alex M: agree. also add a runtime metric for sustained SM% > 90% per-tenant to trigger early throttle
Leah C (CS): which customers were impacted? we saw increased latency for acme-inc and two smaller tenants (tenant-789, tenant-102)
Sam T: impact window ~1739123400 - 1739123620. estimated affected requests: ~3.2k, error uplift minimal (retries), latency increased
Jordan L: handing off to next on-call: @Priya R will continue monitoring for 30m and prepare notes for postmortem
Priya R: taking handoff. will keep this thread updated. saving logs and uploading to incident channel link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1739123456
deploy-bot: rollback not required. no config changes to prod aside from runtime-shim quotas and one pod eviction
ops-bot: incident marked mitigated at 1739123789 — continued monitoring advised
Sam T: thanks team. postmortem owners: Priya (lead), Alex (runtime), Maya (sre), Jordan (cs liaison). Draft due EOD tomorrow
Leah C (CS): CS will reach out to affected customers with a note and offer priority support for 24h
Priya R: closing handoff — will create postmortem draft and attach kernel traces. will include recommended policy changes and timeline. :white_check_mark:
